I don't think so. He does get on his back (with the purpose of scratching it) outside on the lawn, but doesn't make any noise, and goes through a normal motion. There is no rhyme or reason to his movements when he does this on the couch. Sometimes he's just kicking his legs around. Other times he makes a kind of swimming fish motion (which would kind of explain him trying to scratch his back), but for the most part it just looks like some kind of chaotic interpretive dance. When he's doing "his dance" on the couch, he's VERY vocal.

There are a combination of reasons I have come by--my dog, and almost every dog I have had, do the same thing: rolling over is a sign of submission and/or trust, they enjoy it because their body structure doesn't allow them to scratch those areas, it is a sign of play, etc. Does your dog do it until it bleeds, or shows sign of irritation? This could be a sign of an allergy or other medical condition. Mostly it is them playing, itching, and saying, "I'm havin' a fun time playing."

Some of the studies I have passively read about dog behavior indicate that they, especially when younger, are prone to play in the same way as children. Dogs can and will play and engage in "pretend" activities even when not engaged with others'. Your comment also reinforces the idea that your dog enjoys doing it to scratch areas that he/she cannot get to. He/she starts playing, gets excited, and rolls over and has a good ol' time flipping, flopping, and scratching his/her own ass, while engaged in fantasy play.
